statements.status_notes: CVE-2016-9116 is a NULL pointer dereference in an opj_decompress image writer, reported against imagetopnm at convert.c:2226 in OpenJPEG 2.1.2 (that line is in the RAW writer, imagetoraw_common); upstream issue: https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/issues/859. It is a denial of service in the command-line tool when a crafted file is decoded. The reporter confirmed the PoC no longer crashes on later upstream code and the issue was closed. Ubuntu attributes the fix to the AFL hardening merged in https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/0394f8d0f1c981e0bc587beddc14d1fb0b265b1b (pull request 975, first released in 2.2.0) and lists 18.04 and later as not affected: https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2016-9116. Debian's tracker rates it unimportant and records no fixed version. This package builds OpenJPEG 2.5.3, which contains that change. Checked in the shipped 2.5.3 source: opj_j2k_are_all_used_components_decoded() in src/lib/openjp2/j2k.c fails the decode when any requested component has no data (https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg/commit/b2751967ecabf8d8856e85ab91e25d4f235e2eb3, released in 2.4.0), so opj_decompress stops with 'failed to decode image' before any writer can read a NULL component buffer.
